questions.q: A uniform cylindrical rod of length <math><mi>L</mi></math> and radius r, is made from a material whose Young’s modulus of Elasticity equals <math><mi>Y</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When this rod is heated by temperature T and simultaneously subjected to a net longutudinal compressional force F, its length remains unchanged. The coefficient of volume expansion, of the material of the rod, is (nearly) equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Stress =FA
YαT=FA
α=FAYT
γ=3α=3FAYT
γ=3Fπr2YT

questions.q: A cylinder of fixed capacity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>44</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></math> litres contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure. The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of gas in the cylinder by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> will be (Given gas constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At STP volume occupied by one mole of a gas is 22.4 L. Therefore, number of moles are, n=44.822.4=2 mol.

The process is isochoric process as the volume of the cylinder remains fixed and helium is a monatomic gas. Therefore, amount of heat needed will be,

Q=nCvΔT=232R20=3×8.3×20=498 J

questions.q: Two identical metal wires of thermal conductivities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively are connected in series. The effective thermal conductivity of the combination is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Reff=l K1 A+l K2 A=2l KeqA

Keq=2 K1 K2 K1+K2

questions.q: A thermometer graduated according to a linear scale reads a value $x_{0}$ when in contact with boiling water, and $x_{0} / 3$ when in contact with ice. What is the temperature of an object in ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, if this thermometer in the contact with the object reads $x_{0} / 2 ?$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let required temperature $=\mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{6}\&\left(\mathrm{x}_{0}-\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}\right)=\left(100-0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{2 \mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}=100 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{0}=\frac{300}{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{6}=\frac{150}{6}=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

questions.q: When the temperature of a metal wire is increased from 0ºC to 10ºC, its length increases by 0.02%.The percentage change in its mass density will be closed to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Δℓ=ℓαΔt
α=ΔℓℓΔT=0.02100×10;  α=2×10-5
γ=3α=6×10-5
ΔVV=γ×ΔT;  ΔVV×100=6×10-5×10×100=6×10-2
Volume increase by 0.06% therefore density decrease by 0.06%

questions.q: An amount of ice of mass $10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg}$ and temperature $-10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is transformed to vapour of temperature $110^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ by applying heat. The total amount of work required for this conversion is, (Take, specific heat of ice $=2100 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, specific heat of water $=4180 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, specific heat of steam $=1920 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, Latent heat of ice $=3.35 \times 10^5 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}$ and Latent heat of steam $=2.25 \times 10^6\mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_1=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_1 \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 2100 \times 10=21 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_2=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{f}}=10^{-3} \times 3.35 \times 10^5=335 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_3=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{w}} \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 4180 \times 100=418 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_4=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{v}}=10^{-3} \times 2.25 \times 10^6=2250 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_5=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{v}} \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 1920 \times 10=19.2 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{net}}=3043.2 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Resistance of the wire is measured as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> respectively. Temperature coefficient of resistance of the material of the wire is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of a material is related to temperature by expression R=R01+αΔT

Here, at 10°C, we have 2=R01+10α   ...i

And at 30°C, we have 3=R01+30α    ...ii

From equation i, R0=21+10α 

Putting this value in equation ii, 

3=21+10α1+30α⇒3+30α=2+60α

⇒1=30α

Hence, temperature coefficient of the material of wire is α=130=0.033°C-1

questions.q: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of water at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is converted into steam at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> by boiling at atmospheric pressure. The volume of water changes from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> as a liquid to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>671</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> as steam. The change in internal energy of the system during the process will be (Given latent heat of vaporisation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>2257</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, Atmospheric pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open=""><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work to be done in the process is given by

dW=PdV=1×105 Pa×(1.671-0.001) m3=1.670×105 J

The change in heat energy during the vaporisation process can be calculated as follows-

ΔQsupplied =2257×1×103 J=22.57×105 J

Hence, the change in internal energy in the process is given by

ΔU=ΔQsupplied-ΔW=(22.57-1.67)×105 J=20.9×105 J=2090 kJ

questions.q: Each side of a box made of metal sheet in cubic shape is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> at room temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math>, the coefficient of linear expansion of the metal sheet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>. The metal sheet is heated uniformly, by a small temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Δ</mi><mi>T</mi></math>, so that its new temperature is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Δ</mi><mi>T</mi></math>. Calculate the increase in the volume of the metal box.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
ΔV=VγΔT

ΔV=3a3αΔT

questions.q: Three rods of identical cross-section and length are made of three different materials of thermal conductivity K1, K2 and K3, respectively. They are joined together at their ends to make a long rod (see figure). One end of the long rod is maintained at 100°C and the other at 0°C (see figure). If the joints of the rod are at 70°C and 20°C in steady and there is no loss of energy from the surface of the rod, the correct relationship between K1, K2 and K3 is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
K1(100-70)=K2(70-20)=K3(20-0)

K130=K2(50)=K3(20)

⇒K1:K2:K3=10:6:15

K1:K3=2:3

questions.q:
A gun fires a lead bullet of temperature 300 K into a wooden block. The bullet having melting temperature of 600 K penetrates into the block and melts down. If the total heat required for the process is 625 J , then the mass of the bullet is $\qquad$ grams.
(Latent heat of fusion of lead $=2.5 \times 10^4 \mathrm{JKg}^{-1}$ and specific heat capacity of lead $=125 \mathrm{JKg}^{-1}\left.\mathrm{K}^{-1}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 625=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T}+\mathrm{mL} \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}\left[125 \times 300+2.5 \times 10^4\right] \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}[37500+25000] \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}[62500] \\ & \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{M}=10 \text { grams }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two rods $A$ and $B$ of identical dimensions are at temperature $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. If $\mathrm{A}$ is heated upto $180^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ upto $\mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C},$ then the new lengths are the same. If the ratio of the coefficients of linear expansion of $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ is $4: 3,$ then the value of $T$ is
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A heat source at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is connected to another heat reservoir at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> by a copper slab which is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> thick. Given that the thermal conductivity of copper is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.1</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the energy flux through it in the steady-state is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Temperature of heat source, TH=103 K,

Temperature of heat reservoir, TL=102 K,

Conductivity of copper K=0.1 W K-1m-1

From the equation of steady-state heat flow,

dQdt=KA∆TL

Heat energy flux can be defined as the rate of heat energy transfer through a given surface.

1AdQdt=K×1000-1001=90 W m-2

questions.q: The temperature of equal masses of three different liquids <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>y</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>20</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> respectively. The temperature of mixture when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and that when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>26</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The temperature of mixture when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> are mixed will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When A&B are mixed

m1 S1(16-10)=m2 S2(20-16)

6 m1 S1=4 m2 S2    .......(1)

When B&C are mixed

m2 S2(26-20)=m3 S3(30-26)

6 m2 S2=4 m3 S3 ...........(2)

From equation (1) and (2)

9 m1 S1=4 m3 S3

When A&C are mixed

m1 S1( T-10)=m3 S3(30-T)

T=30m3S3+10m1S1m1S1+m3S3

T=103m3S3+m1S1m3S3+m1S1

T=103m3 S3+49 m3 S3m3 S3+49 m3 S3

T=10×3113

=23.84°C

questions.q: A solid metallic cube having total surface area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is uniformly heated. If its temperature is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, calculate the increase in volume of the cube. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total surface area of a cube is 6a2=24 m2⇒a2=4 ⇒a=2 m

Volume of a cube V=a3=8 m3

Change in volume is given by, 

ΔV=V0γΔT, where γ=3α

ΔV=8×1.5×10-4×10 m3⇒ΔV=1.2×105 cm3

questions.q: Two metallic blocks M1 and M2 of same area of cross-section are connected to each other (as shown in figure). If the thermal conductivity of M2 is K then the thermal conductivity of M1 will be : [Assume steady state heat conduction]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let thermal conductivity of M1 be K'.

Using heat current relation for steady state conduction,

K'A100-8016=KA80-08

⇒K'×2016=K×808⇒K'=8K

questions.q: Two identical beakers <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> contain equal volumes of two different liquids at <math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> each and left to cool down. Liquid in <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> has density of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and specific heat of <math><mn>2000</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> while the liquid in <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> has density <math><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and specific heat of <math><mn>4000</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Which of the following best describes their temperature versus time graph schematically? (assume the emissivity of both the beakers to be the same)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Newton's law of cooling,
Rate of cooling: -dTdt=4σeAT03T-T0ms ∝1ms
∴ρA<ρB
mA<mB
And sA<sB
mAsA<mBsB
At  t=0,-dTdtA>-dTdtB
Initially, the rate of cooling for A will be higher than B and temperature (T)  vs time (t) graph will be a curve.

questions.q:
At what temperature a gold ring of diameter 6.230 cm be heated so that it can be fitted on a wooden bangle of diameter 6.241 cm? Both the diameters have been measured at room temperature 27°C.
(Given: coefficient of linear thermal expansion of gold αL=1.4×10-5 K-1)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
To fit gold ring of diameter 5.230 cm over wooden bangle of diameter 6.241 cm, gold ring expansion is required.

So, l=l01+αΔT

⇒6.241=6.2301+1.4×10-5T-27

⇒6.2416.230-1=1.4×10-5T-27

⇒T=152.7°C

questions.q: A cylinder of radius <math><mi>R</mi></math> is surrounded by a cylindrical shell of inner radius <math><mi>R</mi></math> and outer radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi></math>. The thermal conductivity of the material of the inner cylinder is <math><msub><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and that of the outer cylinder is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. Assuming no loss of heat, the effective thermal conductivity of the system for heat flowing along the length of the cylinder is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let q1 and q2 be the rate of flow of heat through inner part from outer part respecting net flow of heat


q=q1+q2

=K1πR2l.ΔT+K2.π2R2-R2l.ΔT

=πR2lΔTK1+3K2

If the cylinder is replaced by a single material of thermal conductivity K then

q=K.2R2l.ΔT

On comparison,

K=K1+3K24.

questions.q: According to law of equipartition of energy the molar specific heat of a diatomic gas at constant volume where the molecule has one additional vibrational mode is :-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A diatomic gas has 5 degrees of freedom apart from vibrational degree of freedom. For each additional vibrational mode, degree of freedom is increased by 2. So new degree of freedom,

f=5+2=7

Therefore, we require molar specific heat capacity at constant volume, which is given by

Cv=f2R=72R

questions.q: A hole is drilled in a metal sheet. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the diameter of hole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. When the sheet is heated to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>177</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the change in the diameter of hole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> . The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> will be _____, if coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Expansion of hole will be similar to that of an imaginary disc.

Let diameter be d0 at 27 °C and d' at 177 °C. Therefore, we can write

d'=d01+αΔT

Therefore, change in diameter will be

⇒d'-d0=5×1.6×10-5×177-27

=12×10-3 cm

Hence, required value of d=12.

questions.q:
Three containers C1,C2 and C3 have water at different temperatures. The table below shows the final temperature T when different amounts of water (given in liters) are taken from each container and mixed (assume no loss of heat during the process)




































C1 C2 C3 T
1l 2l -- 60oC
-- 1l 2l 30oC
2l -- 1l 60oC
1l 1l 1l θ


The value of θ (in oC to the nearest integer) is___________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let θ1, θ2 and θ3 be the temperatures of water in three containers.

1θ1+2θ2+0θ3=1+260
θ1+2θ2=180 …. (1)
0×θ1+1×θ2+2×θ3=1+230
θ2+2θ3=90 …… (2)
2×θ1+0×θ2+1×θ3=2+160
2θ1+θ3=180 …. (3)
and θ1+θ2+θ3=1+1+1θ
from (1)+(2)+(3)
3θ1+3θ2+3θ3=450⟹θ1+θ2+θ3=150
from (4) equation 150=3θ⟹θ=50 °C

questions.q:
Three conductors of same length having thermal conductivity $\mathrm{k}_1, \mathrm{k}_2$ and $\mathrm{k}_3$ are connected as shown in figure.
Area of cross sections of $1^{\text {st }}$ and $2^{\text {nd }}$ conductor are same and for $3^{\text {rd }}$ conductor it is double of the $1^{\text {st }}$ conductor. The temperatures are given in the figure. In steady state condition, the value of $\theta$ is _______ ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. (Given : $\mathrm{k}_1=60 \mathrm{Js}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}, \mathrm{k}_2=120 \mathrm{Js}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}, \mathrm{k}_3=135 \mathrm{Js}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}_1=\frac{2 \mathrm{~L}}{\mathrm{~K}_1 \mathrm{~A}} \\ & \mathrm{R}_2=\frac{2 \mathrm{~L}}{\mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{~A}} \\ & \mathrm{R}_3=\frac{\mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{K}_3 \mathrm{~A}} \\ & \frac{\theta-100}{\frac{\mathrm{R}_1 \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1+\mathrm{R}_2}}+\frac{\theta-0}{\mathrm{R}_3}=0 \\ & \theta=40\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A unit scale is to be prepared whose length does not change with temperature and remains 20 cm, using a bimetallic strip made of brass and iron each of different length. The length of both components would change in such a way that difference between their lengths remains constant. If length of brass is 40 cm and length of iron will be _____ cm.

αiron =1.2×10-5 K-1 and αbrass =1.8×10-5 K-1.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Linear expansion of solid with temperature is given by Lf=L01+α∆T

Here, lB1+αBΔT-li1+αiΔT=lB-li

⇒αBlB=liαi

⇒1.8×10-5×40=li×1.2×10-5

⇒li=1.8×10-5×401.2×10-5=3×402=60

⇒li=60 cm

questions.q:
A water heater of power 2000 W is used to heat water. The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg-1 K-1. The efficiency of heater is 70%. Time required to heat 2 kg of water from 10°C to 60°C is _____ s.

(Assume that the specific heat capacity of water remains constant over the temperature range of the water).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat provided to water will be responsible for increase in temperature. Therefore, we can write

η×P×t=M×s×ΔT

Now, η=70100=0.7 and energy=power×time.

Therefore,

t=2×4200×60°-10°0.7×2000 s=300 s
